title: Fellowship Review
story:
Nora worked in the administrative office of a small research foundation and had recently been handling a batch of fellowship applications. One morning, she received a message that an invited speaker had mistakenly gone to the wrong building and would arrive later than expected. Nora rescheduled the speaker’s seminar for later that afternoon and updated the office calendar.

Once that was settled, she turned to the fellowship applications. She needed to prepare the final folders for two candidates, Chen and Patel. Each folder contained a research proposal, a CV, recommendation letters, and several administrative forms. Nora placed the two folders side by side on her desk and began attaching the candidates’ name labels.

As she was attaching the candidates’ name labels, the office phone rang. Nora answered the call while continuing to work on the folders. During the call, she accidentally attached Chen’s label to Patel’s folder and Patel’s label to Chen’s folder. Not noticing the mistake, she placed both folders with the other completed applications.

Later that morning, Nora attended a staff meeting about the fellowship review schedule. The committee planned to begin evaluating applications the following week, and several staff members discussed how to distribute the files among reviewers. Nora took notes during the meeting and agreed to prepare a spreadsheet showing which reviewer would receive each application.

After the meeting, she returned to her desk and spent some time answering emails. Several applicants had written with questions about when decisions would be announced. Nora replied that the first round of reviews would take approximately two weeks. She then updated the program website with a short notice explaining the expected timeline.

Around lunchtime, Chen called the office to confirm that an additional recommendation letter had arrived. Nora checked the electronic submission system and confirmed that the letter had been received. She told Chen that the application was complete and would soon be forwarded to the review committee.

That afternoon, Patel sent an email asking whether minor formatting changes could still be made to the research proposal. Nora explained that the submission deadline had already passed and that the committee would review the version currently on file. Patel thanked her for the clarification and said no further changes were necessary.

Over the next two days, the office was busy with several unrelated tasks. Nora helped organize a workshop for previous fellowship recipients, prepared reimbursement forms for invited speakers, and assisted a colleague who was updating the foundation’s contact database. She also spent several hours checking whether all fellowship applicants had submitted the required documents.

On Thursday afternoon, another staff member collected the completed application folders from Nora’s desk and placed them in a cabinet for delivery to the review committee. Nora was working on another project at the time and did not reopen the folders. The following morning, the folders were delivered to the committee together with applications from several other candidates.

The committee did not begin reviewing the applications immediately. Its members first met to discuss the evaluation criteria and decide how much weight should be given to research quality, feasibility, and potential impact. Each reviewer was assigned several applications and asked to submit preliminary comments before the next meeting.

Several days later, one of the reviewers began reading Chen’s application. The cover sheet on the folder clearly displayed Chen’s name. However, after opening the folder and beginning to read the research proposal, the reviewer noticed something unexpected: the proposal described a project on urban water management, even though Chen’s stated research area was computational linguistics. The reviewer checked the first page again and saw that the proposal itself was written by Patel.

The reviewer contacted the administrative office to report the problem.

questions.question: What had happened to the invited speaker?
questions.gold_note: The invited speaker had mistakenly gone to the wrong building.

questions.question: What happened while Nora was answering the phone?
questions.gold_note: She accidentally attached Chen’s label to Patel’s folder and Patel’s label to Chen’s folder.

questions.question: How did Patel’s proposal most likely end up in the folder marked with Chen’s name?
questions.gold_note: Nora accidentally switched Chen’s and Patel’s folder labels.
